rationale: Establishing a supply chain risk management team is an organizational act: named people, assigned roles, and a charter for leading and supporting the SCRM activities the plan defines. Nothing in a commit records that a team was established or that the people named accepted the remit. CODEOWNERS is the nearest committed artifact and it is not this — it routes code review by path, which is neither a supply chain remit nor a team, and adjudicating it as evidence here would spend the credibility every other row in this overlay depends on.

citesUpstream.note: Both planes refuse SR-02 (01), and upstream's refusal is the stronger of the two because it is a self-correction: their own `docs/automation-beyond-aws.md` §P5 had listed this control among those build attestation bears on, and their step-8 batch carried it forward, until the adjudication read the control text and found it did not support the claim — the attestation argument belongs to si-7.7 on its detection limb. Cited rather than merely matched, because agreement reached after upstream argued its way OFF a route is worth more than agreement reached without ever considering it, and it is the corroboration our own refusal most needs: CODEOWNERS is the nearest committed artifact and reading it as a supply-chain risk team would spend the credibility every other row depends on. A 3PAO reads the SCRM plan and the team's charter.

externalSystem: Nothing. Collectors take no network by decision, execution is local, and signing is node:crypto — so the supply-chain risk-management plan is read as a committed document rather than through a platform that would itself join the boundary this control is about.
